lesson_title: Two Rivers: The Circular Flow Diagram
hook_text: There are two rivers running through every economy, and they flow in opposite directions.
clip_script: River one carries real things. Your father's work flows from your home to the factory. The school shoes flow from the factory to your home. River two carries money, and it runs the other way. Wages flow from the factory to your home. Your money flows from your home to the shop. Work out, wages in. Shoes in, money out. Every single exchange in the economy has this shape. Now add the government in the middle. Taxes flow straight in from families and businesses. Salaries, grants and spending flow back out. And watch the pipe: some money leaks out, when families save and pay tax. Some flows back in, when businesses invest and the government spends. If the leaks and the taps are equal, the river stays steady. If the leaks win, sales fall and jobs are lost. That is a recession, and now you know where it starts.
visual_style: Two animated rivers circling between labelled boxes, one blue for money and one dotted green for goods and labour, then a pipe with leaks and taps adjusting the water level.
mood: Calm, flowing, with a serious note at the recession.
pacing: Smooth river motion, a crisp rule statement, a slower close on leaks and taps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the diagram in five steps.
